lens: Tremor + shadcn/ui: analytics-heavy, charts everywhere, manager and team insights first
name: Live Coach Studio
one_liner: A call cockpit, not a chat app: the persona talks, an amber coach rail whispers the next move, a live rubric fills in as the call runs, and every score links back to a transcript line. One shadcn/ui system, with Tremor-style analytics confined to the screens where analytics belong.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the lens on analytics and manager-first thinking: Tremor-style KPI, BarList and Tracker patterns, and a team view that is the richest screen in the app. Changed two things. (1) shadcn/ui is the single system of record, not Tremor plus shadcn. Both are Radix, Tailwind and Recharts underneath, so two kits double the theming surface; Tremor blocks are copied in only where they fit the tokens. (2) Charts stay off the live call, the hardest screen. Analytics live in debrief, progress and team. Research: the Mobbin live-call screens and the Second Nature, Hyperbound and Outdoo pages show scoring that either stops when practice ends or runs only after a real call. None of the pages I read show in-call coaching cues during a practice call.

design_language.typography: Geist for UI and headings (600 weight, -0.02em tracking on display sizes). Geist Mono for timers, scores, timestamps and token counts, with tabular numerals. Body 15px over 1.6 on desktop, 16px on mobile. Scale 12, 14, 16, 20, 28, 40. Inter and Sora are dropped.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 10px radius on controls, 16px on cards, 1px hairlines, no glass or blur. Depth comes from tonal surface steps and a 1px ring. The only glow in the product is the amber coach cue. Focus rings are 2px primary with a 2px offset.
design_language.motion: Coach cue slides up 12px and fades in over 180ms. Rubric bars spring-fill over about 600ms. The orb pulses to audio level and flattens when the persona is silent. Under prefers-reduced-motion everything becomes opacity-only.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75px stroke. One custom mark for the coach: a speech bubble with a spark. No emoji in the app or the README.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default. Dark follows the system through next-themes, and the live call defaults to dark so the orb and cue lane stay legible. Both modes are CSS variables on :root with a dark override. Dark values: canvas #0A0F1C, surface #121A2B, ink #E7ECF5, muted #93A0B8, primary #6B8CFF, coach #FBBF24, ai #A78BFA, on-track #4ADE80, at-risk #FB7185.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop: a collapsible left sidebar (shadcn Sidebar, icons only at 1024px) with Practice, Library, New persona, Progress, Team (manager role only) and Settings. A global Cmd+K palette jumps to any persona, scenario or past call. Existing routes stay (/trainer, /trainer/scenarios, /trainer/debrief/[id], /dashboard) so links and README deep links keep working. New routes: /library, /library/[slug], /wizard, /team. Focus mode collapses the sidebar and header during a live call, leaving only the call. Mobile: a bottom tab bar with Practice, Library, Progress and Me. Accounts, MFA and the access code sit under Me. Manager tools sit under Team, not inside Settings, because the lens puts manager insight first.

screens.layout: Full-height Sheet with a four-step header: Source, Draft, Shape, Dry run. live_coaching_and_scoring: Engine: after each finalised turn, the server sends the last six turns, the rubric and the talk-track state to a coach model (GPT-4.1-mini by default) with structured output: next best question, objection type with its trigger quote, current talk-track step, and rubric deltas, each with an evidence line and a status of provisional or confirmed. Target: a cue visible under 2 seconds after the rep stops speaking. The coach never writes to the persona's channel. v1 cues are visual only, so the persona cannot hear them. Modes: Silent, Light (objections and step changes only), Full. Live scores use the same grader prompt as the debrief, so they differ only in whether a quote is confirmed. If the coach times out, the cue lane shows 'Coach paused' and the call continues. Self-score D: 6.5. Above baseline on the evidence links and the no-leak design; not higher, because live scoring is not yet checked against human raters.
persona_library_and_wizard: Persona files are YAML in /personas/<job>/<slug>.yaml, validated by the same zod schema the wizard uses, so a contributor's file and an AI draft have identical shape. Launch target: 15 sales jobs (SDR cold call, AE discovery, SaaS, insurance, mortgage, real estate, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections), 120 personas in total. Forty are reviewed at v1 and the rest carry a Draft badge. Filters: job, industry, difficulty, call type and objection type. Every persona gets a review checklist for stereotyping, especially in insurance, mortgage and auto. The wizard runs four steps (Source, Draft, Shape, Dry run) and turns a job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP or pasted call into a persona, scenario and rubric, with every field traced to its source sentence. Self-score E: 6.0. The generation path is strong; the review load of 120 personas is the real cost.
signature_moments: A cue lane that shows one amber cue at a time, with the trigger quote it came from printed beneath it.
Rubric fills that start hatched as provisional and turn solid only when a transcript quote confirms them.
A call timeline strip in the debrief: one tick per turn, coloured by criterion, clickable to replay that moment.
A violet provenance chip on every AI output showing the model, latency and token count.
A calibration chart that sets AI score against manager score for each call.
A wizard draft that highlights the exact job-description or CRM sentence behind each persona field.
openai_fund_angle: OpenAI use is visible and auditable. Each debrief footer reads 'Graded by GPT-4.1-mini, 9 turns, with token count and latency'. An in-app Models page lists which OpenAI model runs grading, coaching, the persona wizard and the optional Realtime voice engine. The README hero carries the text 'Built with OpenAI models' with no logo, pending brand approval. Codex is the contributor path: AGENTS.md at the repo root; a 'Contribute a persona' button opens a prefilled YAML PR template and a Codex CLI prompt; a Codex-powered PR review action checks persona files against the zod schema; release notes are drafted with Codex. These map to the program's named fits: PR review, maintainer automation and release workflows. Apply to the Codex open source fund (grants up to $25,000 in API credits for projects using Codex CLI and OpenAI models) and to Codex for Open Source. The program page excerpt mentions six months of an additional benefit without detail, so confirm terms before applying.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0 (about 1 week): tokens on :root, shadcn init, Geist, and the Sidebar and Command shell replacing the glass header. Existing routes stay. Phase 1: Landing, library with the faceted filter, pre-call briefing, and the live call with the coach rail behind a feature flag. Phase 2: debrief timeline and scorecard, progress dashboard, and the persona wizard. Phase 3: team view and calibration, which need Prisma-backed org data. Scenarios stay in localStorage until the database move in Phase 3. Tailwind 3.4 stays in phase 1; the move to Tailwind 4 comes later as its own change so it does not mix with the redesign.

risks: Latency and cost: a coach call on every turn adds tokens to every session. Cap it with Light mode and a per-call budget, and show the cost in the debrief footer.
Coach leakage: any audio whisper routed to the persona's microphone breaks the scenario. v1 stays visual-only.
Persona bias: insurance, mortgage and auto personas can stereotype. Nothing leaves Draft without the review checklist.
Recording consent: voice calls are recorded. Gate the Realtime and ElevenLabs paths behind jurisdiction-aware consent before they go live.
Look drift: shadcn is common, and without a distinct chart and cue language the app reads as another default template.
Review load: 120 personas is a lot to review. Ship 40 reviewed personas and label the rest as drafts.
Fund eligibility: the fund asks for Codex CLI and OpenAI model use, and the program page excerpt mentions a six-month benefit without detail. Verify terms before applying.
